items.title: Ellen Rowe interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 2, 2024
items.q: she used to do these portraits of her guests sometimes on the Piano Jazz show. And she did a portrait of Dudley Moore.

ctx.x: Exactly. Yeah. I remember like cassette recordings I had of Marian McPartland when I was trying to transcribe her solo piano albums and you know it was push and rewind and

push and rewind and push and rewind. And you know the other beauty about that was that — one tape I remember in particular was running almost a half-step sharp and I transcribed a solo piece for — it was, she used to do these portraits of her guests sometimes on the Piano Jazz show. And she did a portrait of Dudley Moore. And I painstakingly took that sucker down. I could not believe she had played in C sharp minor but you know she was Marian, she could play in any key. And sure enough she goes, “I could never…
Who are the great masters for 20-year-olds now? I mean we moved from generation to generation. You know Coltrane was the zenith for many years. Who do they cite now as their influences?
